summary: Iter-32 verified page-level LOCK and per-page dated version HISTORY end-to-end. Backend 14/14 pytest pass in ~43s (test_iter32_page_lock_history.py). Covered: (a) POST /apps/{id}/pages/{pid}/lock owner-happy path — toggles both directions, persists on GET /pages, writes >=2 activity entries kind='page.lock', 404 on a bogus page_id. (b) Permission matrix on a THROWAWAY tenant with registered editor/viewer/admin members — editor+viewer both get 403 'Only the agency owner or an admin can lock or unlock pages', admin can lock+unlock. (c) Lock enforcement on the PATCH page endpoint — editor 423 with the page name in the message and blocks byte-identical after; owner AND admin still succeed (matches the user's explicit choice). Same rule applies to POST /pages/{pid}/versions/{vid}/restore. (d) Version history is PRE-SAVE: after saves at baseline/b1/b2/b3, the newest version's full blocks contain 'save-2' (the state BEFORE 'save-3'), the live page has 'save-3'; list is newest-first with reason 'save', by, sections, created_at and max=30. (e) Version cap: 33 quick saves leave exactly 30 rows in db.page_versions and 30 in the GET response. (f) GET /versions/{vid} returns the full blocks array unchanged, does NOT mutate the live page, and 404s with 'no longer available' on unknown ids. (g) Restore round-trip: restoring an older version updates the live blocks, creates a 'before restore' snapshot, refreshes apps.site_snapshot.headline, logs 'page.restored', and restoring the 'before restore' version gets the previous state back. (h) Wholesale-rewrite snapshots: /site/import (mode=replace) writes 'before import from https://example.com' snapshots for the pre-existing page_ids; /site/premium-rebuild writes 'before ... rebuild'; /ai/generate-site writes 'before AI site generation'. (i) Cross-tenant isolation — POST /lock with a page_id from another tenant 404s, GET /versions returns [], and a viewer of tenant A cannot GET /versions on tenant B. Frontend smoke on Studio Booking (app_e3cb4f084785): SITE MODE tab renders 4 page-lock buttons (page-lock-home / -about / -services / -contact), padlock click toggles amber colour (class text-amber-400) and shows the toasts 'Home locked — clients can no longer edit it' and 'Home unlocked'. page-history-btn opens the HistoryDialog showing dated versions with sections, author, reason and a 'LATEST' chip on the newest. history-preview-0 loads that version into the canvas and shows the 'Previewing the ... version — nothing is saved until you restore it' banner with a 'Save changes' button (dirty-but-unsaved as specified). No 'Uncaught runtime errors' overlay. Regression: tenant content lock still works (iter-31 file untouched); Overview snapshot sync still fires on page save; no double-writes were observed (single 'page.saved' activity per PATCH, single snapshot per PATCH).

minor.issue: 'before import from ...' snapshots are stored against the OLD page_ids, but replace mode DELETES those pages so their page_ids no longer appear in GET /pages. The current UI lists versions per existing page_id, so these snapshots are orphaned and NOT restorable through Site Mode. The data is there in db.page_versions, so recovery is possible via API, but the UI cannot undo a whole import today. Flag for main agent — either surface an 'Undo last import' entry point in Site Mode that lists orphaned reasons ('before import from …'), or re-attach snapshots to slugs so replace-mode restores can find them.

minor.endpoint: GET /apps/{id}/pages/{page_id}/versions with a page_id from another tenant
minor.issue: Returns 200 {versions: []} rather than 404. Behaviour is safe (no data leak), but a 404 would be more consistent with the lock endpoint. Optional.

action_items: Expose orphaned 'before import from …' / 'before … rebuild' / 'before AI site generation' snapshots in the History UI so a user can actually undo a whole import / rebuild / AI regen — currently those snapshots are stored against page_ids that replace-mode deleted, so the History dialog (which is per existing page_id) never shows them. Options: (1) list per-slug in the dialog and match on slug in restore, (2) add a top-level 'Undo last <import/rebuild/AI>' action on the Site Mode toolbar that reads reasons starting with 'before ' and restores the whole batch.
critical_code_review_comments: page_guard.snapshot() uses `.skip(MAX_VERSIONS).to_list(200)` — the 200 cap is fine because pruning runs after every save, but if a legacy tenant has >230 versions the prune will only delete the oldest 200 in one pass. Non-blocking; add a comment or an outer while-loop for peace of mind.

page_guard.restore_version imports content_lock.sync_overview inline. Fine, but the same pattern in studio.update_page (line 226) already does it — consider hoisting the import to module scope for both to avoid the runtime import cost on every save/restore.

GET /apps/{id}/pages/{page_id}/versions does NOT verify that the page_id belongs to app_id — it just queries by both. That's safe for versions (composite key) but returns 200/[] on cross-tenant page_ids; consider a 404 if `db.pages.find_one({app_id, page_id})` is None for parity with the lock endpoint.
restore_version does `snapshot(prev)` then `pages.update_one` — if the update fails the snapshot is orphaned. Not a data-loss risk but leaves a spurious 'before restore' entry. Minor.

web_import.apply_import calls snapshot_site BEFORE deleting pages, which is correct, but the snapshots keep the deleted page_ids. As noted above, the UI can't currently reach them for undo — either link snapshots to slugs (stable across replace) or add an undo affordance.

rca of the issue: Import/rebuild/AI snapshot orphan issue reproduction: (1) On a THROWAWAY tenant, unlock content-lock and note the home page_id X. (2) POST /site/import {url:example.com, mode:replace, max_pages:1}. (3) After job done, GET /pages — new page_ids are returned, X is gone. (4) db.page_versions still has a row with page_id=X and reason='before import from https://example.com'. (5) GET /apps/{id}/pages/{new_pid}/versions does NOT include this row (different page_id). Fix options: (a) store snapshots against slug rather than page_id, or (b) add a batch-restore endpoint keyed by reason that re-creates deleted pages in one shot.
